notes.headline: ORIX: half-year profit triples to ¥856 billion on a ¥796 billion paper gain from Toshiba’s Kioxia stake; underlying income up 4%
notes.takeaway: Net income for the six months to September jumped 216% to ¥856.2 billion, almost entirely because ORIX’s stake in the Toshiba buyout vehicle booked ¥795.7 billion of gains on Kioxia shares. Operating income rose only 3.9%, ORIX left its forecast unchanged, raised its interim dividend to ¥113.56, and the ADRs fell 2%.
results: ORIX Corporation reported total revenue of ¥1,673.9 billion for the six months ended September 30, up 9.6%, and operating income of ¥239.5 billion, up 3.9%. Income from continuing operations before tax rose 195% to ¥1,117.9 billion and net income attributable to shareholders 215.8% to ¥856.2 billion. Comprehensive income rose 68.9% to ¥825.0 billion.

The surge came from ¥795.7 billion of equity-method income through TB Investment Limited Partnership, the vehicle through which ORIX participated in the 2023 take-private of Toshiba. Toshiba recorded large gains on sales and revaluation of its shares in memory-chip maker Kioxia in the March and June quarters, and ORIX books its share.

ORIX has decided to sell ORIX Bank, which is now classified as held for sale and reported as a discontinued operation; prior-year figures were restated. The interim dividend rose to ¥113.56 from ¥93.76.
mgmt: ORIX cautioned that although the Kioxia-related gains are substantial, they will fluctuate with Kioxia’s share price, remain uncertain, and do not bring ORIX any corresponding cash. It said such gains are treated separately from its ordinary results for the purpose of its shareholder-return policy, and it did not revise its full-year earnings or dividend forecasts.

The company highlighted continued growth across its diversified businesses, which span leasing, real estate, insurance, environment and energy, private equity investment and aircraft and ship finance, and the disposal of ORIX Bank as part of an ongoing effort to recycle capital into higher-return activities.
view: The headline profit is a mirage in the sense that matters for shareholders: ORIX did not receive ¥796 billion and will not unless the Toshiba consortium eventually sells Kioxia shares and distributes the proceeds. It is a paper gain on an indirect holding, created by the memory-chip boom that has sent Kioxia’s shares soaring along with Sandisk and Micron. ORIX’s own disclosure is admirably clear about this, and its decision not to change its forecast or its dividend policy shows management is not treating the gain as earning power.

Underneath, the business is growing slowly. Operating income up 3.9% and revenue up 9.6% describe a steady, diversified financial conglomerate rather than a growth company. The sale of ORIX Bank is the more meaningful strategic signal: management has been under pressure to lift return on equity toward 11% and above, and selling a low-return deposit-funded bank frees capital for buybacks or higher-return investments in areas like renewable energy and private equity.

The Kioxia stake is nevertheless real value. If the consortium crystallises gains — through Toshiba’s sale of Kioxia shares or a future Toshiba relisting — ORIX could receive substantial cash that would support larger buybacks. That optionality, plus a valuation of about five times this year’s inflated earnings, explains why investors who look past the headline see ORIX as cheap. The risk is that memory-chip prices turn and the paper gains reverse as quickly as they appeared.
notes.watch: Watch Kioxia’s share price and any Toshiba sale of Kioxia shares, the completion of the ORIX Bank sale and use of the proceeds, and progress toward ORIX’s return-on-equity target.
